description: Read one file or up to 1000, whole or as a line slice. Use when you know the path. Do not use it to check size or existence; use `stat` instead. To locate content, use `search_text`, `find_files`, or `list`. Only whole reads return images and audio as media; other binary files fail with BINARY_FILE unless binary: true. Past the size limit, a whole read fails with TOO_LARGE; a single-path head or range is truncated. A batch shares a 512 KiB budget: an overflowing file is skipped and later files still read. isError means every path failed. Pick one slice (head, tail, or startLine/endLine); it applies to every batch file. Returns text plus per-path results[]: an error, or linesRead, hasMoreLines, continuation args, modified, optional contentHash. Full reads add totalLines; a tail gets no continuation.

binary.description: Return a non-image, non-audio binary file as a base64 resource. Whole reads only. Without it, such a file fails with BINARY_FILE.

head.description: First N lines. Not with tail or startLine/endLine.

includeHash.description: Include SHA-256 of the returned content (the slice for a partial read).

lineNumbers.description: Prefix each line with its number and a tab. Not with tail. Leave the prefix out of edit text.

path.description: Single file path; mutually exclusive with paths

paths.description: Array of file paths for batch mode (max 1000); mutually exclusive with path

items.description: File or directory path inside an allowed workspace root.

startLine.description: First line, 1-based. Without endLine, reads to the end.

tail.description: Last N lines. Not with head, startLine/endLine, or lineNumbers.

name: read
title: Read File
